ko.title: [소매 입문 #7] Trader Joe's는 4,000개 항목을 판매합니다. Walmart는 100,000개를 판매합니다. 둘 다 승리하고 있습니다.

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > 소매 전략은 함께 이루어지는 세 가지 결정입니다: 누구를 대상으로 할 것인지, 그들에게 무엇을 어떻게 팔 것인지, 그리고 5년 후에도 그 우위가 유지될 이유가 무엇인지입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람들은 소매 전략이 '좋은 위치를 선택하고 가격 경쟁에서 지지 않는다'는 의미라고 생각합니다.

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: 그것은 전술입니다.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: 전략은 그것보다 상위 계층입니다.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: 소매 교과서에서 **소매 전략**은 세 가지 질문에 답하는 진술입니다:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **목표 시장** — 우리는 어떤 고객을 겨냥하고 있습니까?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **소매 형식** — 그들을 충족시키기 위해 어떤 형태의 소매를 구축할 것인가?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **지속 가능한 경쟁 우위** — 경쟁사가 모방하기 어렵게 만들 것은 무엇인가?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: *지속 가능한*이라는 단어가 질문 3에서 핵심 역할을 합니다.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: 모든 경쟁사가 화요일 할인을 수요일에 따라잡을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: 실제로 지속되는 우위들은 일반적으로 소수의 영역에서 나옵니다: 고객 충성도와 습관, 경쟁사가 획득할 수 없는 물리적 위치, 당신이 통제하는 독특한 상품, 유통 및 정보 시스템, 공급업체 관계, 그리고 직원 채용 및 유지 방식.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: 가격 인하는 그 목록에 포함되지 않습니다.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: 질문 2의 형식은 **소매 믹스**에서 나옵니다 — 소매업체가 사용하는 6가지 수단이며, 이들은 모두 같은 방향을 가리켜야 합니다:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **상품 구성** — 카테고리 수(폭), 각 카테고리 내 선택의 수(깊이)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **가격 책정** — 매일 저가, 상향-하향 프로모션, 프리미엄

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **위치** — 쇼핑몰, 스트립 센터, 다운타운, 온라인 전용

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **매장 디자인 및 디스플레이** — 레이아웃, 분위기, 한 손으로 운반할 수 있는 양

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **고객 서비스** — 직원 헬프데스크 vs. 셀프 체크아웃 vs. 챗봇

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **커뮤니케이션** — 광고, 이메일, 충성도 프로그램, 소셜

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: 이 6가지를 설정하면 **포지셔닝**을 만들게 됩니다: 당신의 매장이 쇼핑객의 머리 속에서 다른 대안들에 비해 차지하는 위치.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: 포지셔닝은 당신이 쓰는 슬로건이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: 그것은 당신이 실제로 한 6가지 선택의 결과입니다.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: 불편한 점은 믹스가 *내부적으로 일관되어야*한다는 것입니다.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: 깊은 구성에 저가를 더하고, 높은 서비스를 더하고, 최적의 부동산을 더하는 것은 전략이 아닙니다 — 그것은 위시리스트이고 손실을 초래합니다.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: 모든 강한 소매업체는 의도적으로 어떤 분야에서는 눈에 띄게 약합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활에서

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: 오하이오주 콜럼버스에 살고 있고, 15분 운전 거리 내에 4가지 식료품점 옵션이 있다고 가정해봅시다.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: 같은 도시, 같은 쇼핑객, 하지만 4가지 완전히 다른 전략.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's**는 대략 4,000개 항목을 취급합니다.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: 일반적인 슈퍼마켓은 30,000개 이상을 취급합니다.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's 선반에 있는 대부분의 상품은 자체 프라이빗 레이블이고, 로열티 카드도 없고, 주간 광고지도 없으며, 매장은 작습니다 — 새로운 메인 점포보다는 종종 오래되고 저렴한 소매 공간에 위치합니다.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: 일관성에 주목하세요: 좁은 구성은 항목당 높은 판매량을 의미하고, 이는 더 나은 단위 원가를 의미하고, 이것이 전문적으로 느껴지는 상품에 $3.99라는 가격을 책정할 수 있게 해줍니다.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: 그들의 우위는 문자 그대로 다른 곳에서는 구입할 수 없는 독특한 상품이며, 충분히 작은 매장이어서 전체 쇼핑에 20분이 걸린다는 것입니다.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: 목표 시장: 누군가 다른 사람이 자신들을 위해 선택을 정해주는 것을 선호하는 쇼핑객들.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**는 2마일 떨어져 있으며 훨씬 더 엄격합니다.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: 제품은 배송 상자 그대로 있고, 동전으로 카트를 임차하고, 직접 식료품을 포장하고 자신의 가방을 가져와야 합니다.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: 이들 각각은 제거되는 비용이고 가격으로 전가됩니다.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: 목표 시장: 최고 우선순위가 영수증 하단의 합계인 쇼핑객들.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter**는 반대 방향으로 나아갑니다 — 막대한 구성, 식료품 플러스 타이어 플러스 TV, 좁은 구성이 아니라 수십 년에 걸쳐 구축된 공급 체인 및 정보 시스템에 의해 지원되는 매일의 저가.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: 그것은 수십억 달러의 인프라로 측정되는 우위이며, 정확히 그것이 지속 가능한 이유입니다.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods**는 더 높은 가격을 청구하고 그것에 만족합니다: 준비된 음식, 직원 카운터, 공급 기준, 고소득 거래 지역의 위치.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: 이제 핵심입니다.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: 이 4개 중 어느 것도 '최고의 식료품점'이 아니며, 어느 것도 다른 것들을 자신들의 게임에서 이기려고 노력하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's는 Walmart이 더 큰 시리얼 코너를 가질 때 지지 않습니다 — 좁은 코너가 전략입니다.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: 소매업체가 *실제로* 한 번에 4가지를 모두 하려고 시도할 때, 믹스는 일관성을 잃고, 포지셔닝은 흐려지고, 쇼핑객들은 그 매장이 무엇을 위한 것인지 말할 수 없게 됩니다.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: 그것이 실패한 체인에 대한 일반적인 부검입니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. 소매 전략 = 목표 시장 + 소매 형식 + 실제로 모방하기 어려운 경쟁 우위.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. 형식은 6가지 믹스 수단(구성, 가격, 위치, 디자인, 서비스, 커뮤니케이션)으로 구축되며, 이들은 서로 일관되어야 합니다.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. 포지셔닝은 고객의 마음속에서 이러한 선택들의 결과입니다. 일부 분야에서 의도적으로 약한 것이 다른 분야에서 강해지게 하는 것입니다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자체 퀴즈

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **소매 전략** — 소매업체의 목표 시장, 그 시장에 서비스를 제공하기 위해 사용할 형식, 그리고 지속 가능한 경쟁 우위의 기반을 명시하는 진술.

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **목표 시장** — 소매업체가 자신의 자원과 소매 믹스를 향하는 특정 고객 세그먼트.

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **소매 형식** — 소매업체의 제안의 특성으로, 구성, 가격, 위치, 디자인, 서비스, 커뮤니케이션의 믹스로 정의됩니다.

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **소매 믹스** — 소매업체가 그 형식을 구축하기 위해 결합하는 6가지 제어 가능한 수단.

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **포지셔닝** — 소매업체가 경쟁사에 비해 고객들의 마음속에 차지하는 이미지로, 소매 믹스에 의해 생성됩니다.

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **지속 가능한 경쟁 우위** — 경쟁사가 쉽게 복제할 수 없기 때문에 시간이 지남에 따라 유지될 수 있는 우위.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *답: **Q1 → B.** 가격 인하는 소매에서 복사하기 가장 쉬운 움직임입니다 — 경쟁사가 다음 날 아침에 따라잡을 수 있으므로, 그것은 우위가 아닌 판매량을 사줍니다.

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: 위치, 독점 상품, 공급 체인 인프라는 모두 복제하는 데 수년과 자본이 필요합니다.

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **Q2 → X (거짓).** 믹스의 각 요소에는 비용이 들고, 깊은 구성과 높은 서비스는 비용 구조를 높이며, 이는 가장 낮은 가격을 유지하는 것을 불가능하게 만듭니다.

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: 일관된 전략은 무엇에서 약할지 선택하는 것을 요구합니다.

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **Q3 → A.** 폭(또는 다양성) = 카테고리 수, 깊이 = 카테고리 내 SKU 수.

segments.src: Trader Joe's is moderate in breadth and deliberately shallow in depth.*
segments.tr: Trader Joe's는 폭에서는 중간 정도이고 깊이에서는 의도적으로 얕습니다.*

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > 零售战略是一起做出的三个决定：你为谁服务，你将卖给他们什么以及如何卖，以及为什么这种优势在五年后仍然存在。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: 大多数人认为零售战略意味着"选择一个好位置，不要被压低价格"。

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: 那是战术。

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: 战略是在其之上的层次。

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: 在零售教科书中，**零售战略**是回答三个问题的陈述：

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **目标市场** — 我们针对的是哪些客户？

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **零售模式** — 我们将建立什么样的服务来满足他们？

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **可持续竞争优势** — 什么将使竞争对手难以复制？

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: *可持续*这个词在第3个问题中发挥了真正的作用。

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: 任何竞争对手都可以在第二天早上就配对你的折扣。

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: 真正持久的优势往往来自于一小部分地方：客户忠诚度和习惯、竞争对手无法获得的实体地点、你控制的独特商品、配销和信息系统、供应商关系，以及你如何招聘和留任员工。

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: 降价不在这个清单上。

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: 第2个问题中的格式是从**零售组合**构建的——零售商拉动的六个杠杆，所有这些都必须指向同一方向：

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **商品组合** — 有多少个类别（广度），每个类别内有多少个选择（深度）

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **定价** — 日常低价、高低促销、高端

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **位置** — 商场、条形中心、市中心、仅在线

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **店铺设计和展示** — 布局、氛围、你一只手能拿多少

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **客户服务** — 有人值班的帮助台vs.自助结账vs.聊天机器人

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **沟通** — 广告、电子邮件、忠诚度计划、社交

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: 设定这六个，你就产生了一个**位置**：相对于替代品，你的商店在购物者心中占据的位置。

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: 定位不是你写的标语。

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: 这是你实际做出的六个选择的结果。

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: 令人不适的部分是这个组合必须是*内部一致的*。

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: 深度商品组合加低价加高服务加黄金地产不是战略——那是一个愿望清单，会亏钱。

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: 每个强大的零售商都明显地故意在某些方面做得很差。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: 假设你住在俄亥俄州哥伦布市，在十五分钟的车程内有四个杂货店选择。

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: 同样的城市，同样的购物者，四个完全不同的答案。

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** 大约销售4,000种商品。

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: 常规超市销售30,000种或更多。

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: TJ's货架上的大部分商品是其自有私有标签，没有忠诚卡，没有每周传单，商店很小——通常在较旧、较便宜的零售空间而不是新的锚点购物中心。

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: 注意这种一致性：狭窄的商品组合意味着每件商品的高销量，这意味着更好的单位成本，这支撑了$3.99的高端商品价格。

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: 他们的优势是你无法在其他地方购买的独特商品，加上一个足够小的商店，完整的购物之旅只需要二十分钟。

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: 目标市场：宁愿让别人为他们编辑选择的购物者。

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**，距离两英里，更加严格。

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: 产品保持在运输纸箱中，你用一枚硬币租用购物车，你自己装袋杂货并自带购物袋。

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: 这些中的每一项都是一个被移除并转入价格的成本。

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: 目标：购物者的首要优先事项是收据底部的总数。

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **沃尔玛超级中心**走相反的路——庞大的商品组合、杂货加轮胎加电视、日常低价由多年建立的供应链和信息系统资助，而不是由小组合资助。

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: 这是一个以数十亿美元基础设施衡量的优势，这正是为什么它是可持续的。

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** 收费更高，这没关系：准备好的食品、有人值班的柜台、采购标准、高收入贸易地区的位置。

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: 现在是关键点。

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: 这四个中没有一个是"最好的杂货店"，也没有人试图在自己的游戏中打败其他人。

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: 当沃尔玛有更大的麦片通道时，Trader Joe's 并没有损失——狭窄的通道本身就是战略。

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: 当零售商*确实*试图同时成为这四个时，组合变得不一致，位置变得模糊，购物者停止能够说出商店是为了什么。

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: 这是对失败连锁店的常见尸检。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行回顾

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. 零售战略 = 目标市场 + 零售模式 + 实际上难以复制的竞争优势。

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. 该格式是从六个组合杠杆建立的——商品组合、价格、位置、设计、服务、沟通——它们必须相互一致。

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. 定位是客户心中这些选择的结果；在某些领域故意虚弱是使你在其他领域强大的原因。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **零售战略** — 对零售商的目标市场、用来服务该市场的格式以及其可持续竞争优势基础的陈述。

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **目标市场** — 零售商将其资源和零售组合指向的特定客户细分。

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **零售模式** — 零售商服务的性质，由其商品组合、价格、位置、设计、服务和沟通的组合定义。

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **零售组合** — 零售商结合以构建该模式的六个可控杠杆。

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **定位** — 零售商在客户心中相对于竞争对手的形象，由其零售组合产生。

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **可持续竞争优势** — 可以随时间维持的优势，因为竞争对手无法轻易复制它。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 → B.** 降价是零售中最容易复制的举动——竞争对手可以在第二天早上就配对它，所以它买的是数量，而不是优势。

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: 地点、专有商品和供应链基础设施都需要多年和资本才能复制。

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **Q2 → X (错误).** 组合的每个元素都有成本；深度商品组合和高服务提高了成本结构，这使得最低价格无法维持。

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: 连贯的战略需要选择在什么方面虚弱。

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **Q3 → A.** 广度（或多样性）= 类别数；深度 = 类别内的SKU数。

segments.src: Trader Joe's is moderate in breadth and deliberately shallow in depth.*
segments.tr: Trader Joe's 在广度上是中等的，在深度上故意很浅。*

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: अधिकांश लोग सोचते हैं कि खुदरा रणनीति का मतलब है "एक अच्छा स्थान चुनें और कीमत पर कटौती न हों।"

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: यह रणकौशल है।

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: रणनीति इसके ऊपर की परत है।

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: खुदरा पाठ्यपुस्तकों में, एक **खुदरा रणनीति** एक कथन है जो तीन प्रश्नों का उत्तर देता है:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **लक्ष्य बाजार** — हम किन ग्राहकों को लक्ष्य कर रहे हैं?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **खुदरा प्रारूप** — उनकी सेवा के लिए हम कौन सा प्रस्ताव बनाएँगे?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **टिकाऊ प्रतिस्पर्धी लाभ** — क्या प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के लिए इसकी नकल करना मुश्किल बनाएगा?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: शब्द *टिकाऊ* प्रश्न 3 में वास्तविक काम कर रहा है।

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: कोई भी प्रतिद्वंद्वी आपकी मंगलवार की छूट को बुधवार तक मैच कर सकता है।

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: जो लाभ वास्तव में स्थायी होते हैं, वे आमतौर पर कुछ स्रोतों से आते हैं: ग्राहक निष्ठा और आदत, भौतिक स्थान जो प्रतिद्वंद्वियों को नहीं मिल सकते, अद्वितीय माल जिसे आप नियंत्रित करते हैं, वितरण और सूचना प्रणाली, आपूर्तिकर्ता संबंध, और कर्मचारियों को कैसे नियुक्त करते हैं और रखते हैं।

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: कीमत में कटौती उस सूची में नहीं है।

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: प्रश्न 2 में प्रारूप **खुदरा मिश्रण** से बनाया जाता है — छह लीवर जो एक खुदरा विक्रेता खींचता है, जो सभी को एक ही दिशा में इंगित करना चाहिए:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **माल की छँटाई** — कितनी श्रेणियाँ (चौड़ाई), प्रत्येक के अंदर कितनी पसंद (गहराई)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **मूल्य निर्धारण** — रोजमर्रा की कम कीमत, उच्च-निम्न प्रचार, प्रीमियम

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **स्थान** — मॉल, स्ट्रिप सेंटर, डाउनटाउन, केवल ऑनलाइन

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **स्टोर डिजाइन और डिस्प्ले** — लेआउट, माहौल, आप एक हाथ में कितना ले जा सकते हैं

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **ग्राहक सेवा** — कर्मचारी सहायता डेस्क बनाम स्व-चेकआउट बनाम चैटबॉट

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **संचार** — विज्ञापन, ईमेल, वफादारी कार्यक्रम, सामाजिक

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: उन छह को सेट करें, और आपने एक **स्थिति** तैयार की है: वह स्थान जो आपकी दुकान एक खरीदार के दिमाग में विकल्पों के सापेक्ष कब्जा करती है।

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: स्थिति एक नारा नहीं है जो आप लिखते हैं।

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप कोलंबस, ओहियो में रहते हैं, और पंद्रह मिनट की ड्राइव के भीतर चार किराने के विकल्प हैं।

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: एक ही शहर, एक ही खरीदार, चार पूरी तरह से अलग जवाब।

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** लगभग 4,000 आइटम रखता है।

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: एक पारंपरिक सुपरमार्केट 30,000 या अधिक रखता है।

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: TJ की शेल्फ पर अधिकांश चीजें इसका अपना निजी लेबल हैं, कोई वफादारी कार्ड नहीं है, कोई साप्ताहिक विज्ञापन नहीं है, और दुकानें छोटी हैं — अक्सर नए एंकर स्टोर की तुलना में पुरानी, सस्ती खुदरा जगह में।

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: सामंजस्य पर ध्यान दें: एक संकीर्ण छँटाई का मतलब प्रति आइटम उच्च मात्रा है, जिसका मतलब प्रति यूनिट बेहतर लागत है, जो कुछ विशेष महसूस करने वाली चीज पर $3.99 की कीमत को संभव बनाता है।

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: उनका लाभ अद्वितीय माल है जिसे आप शाब्दिक रूप से कहीं और नहीं खरीद सकते, साथ ही एक दुकान इतनी छोटी है कि एक पूरी यात्रा बीस मिनट लेती है।

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: लक्ष्य बाजार: वे खरीदार जो किसी और को उनके लिए विकल्पों को छाँटना पसंद करते हैं।

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**, दो मील दूर, अभी भी और कठोर है।

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: उत्पाद शिपिंग कार्टन में ही रहते हैं, आप एक चौथाई के साथ कार्ट किराए पर लेते हैं, आप अपने किराने का सामान स्वयं बैग करते हैं और अपने स्वयं के बैग लाते हैं।

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: उन सभी में से हर एक एक लागत है जो हटाई गई और कीमत में पास की गई है।

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: लक्ष्य: वे खरीदार जिनकी शीर्ष प्राथमिकता रसीद के तल पर कुल है।

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** विपरीत दिशा में जाता है — विशाल छँटाई, किराने के सामान प्लस टायर प्लस टीवी, रोजमर्रा की कम कीमत जो छोटी छँटाई से नहीं बल्कि दशकों में निर्मित आपूर्ति श्रृंखला और सूचना प्रणाली द्वारा वित्तपोषित है।

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: यह बुनियादी ढाँचे के अरबों डॉलर में मापा जाने वाला लाभ है, जो बिल्कुल यही कारण है कि यह टिकाऊ है।

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** अधिक चार्ज करता है और इसके साथ ठीक है: तैयार खाद्य, कर्मचारी काउंटर, सोर्सिंग मानक, उच्च आय वाले व्यापार क्षेत्रों में स्थान।

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: अब मुख्य बिंदु।

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: इन चारों में से कोई भी "सर्वश्रेष्ठ किराना स्टोर" नहीं है, और कोई भी दूसरों को उनके अपने खेल में हराने की कोशिश नहीं कर रहा है।

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's नहीं हार रहा है जब Walmart के पास एक बड़ा अनाज का गलियारा है — एक संकीर्ण गलियारा ही रणनीति है।

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: जब एक खुदरा विक्रेता *वास्तव में* एक बार सभी चार होने की कोशिश करता है, तो मिश्रण असंगत हो जाता है, स्थिति धुंधली हो जाती है, और खरीदार यह कहने में सक्षम होना बंद कर देते हैं कि दुकान किसके लिए है।

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: यह एक विफल श्रृंखला पर सामान्य शव परीक्षा है।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति पुनरावृत्ति

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. खुदरा रणनीति = लक्ष्य बाजार + खुदरा प्रारूप + एक प्रतिस्पर्धी लाभ जो वास्तव में नकल करना मुश्किल है।

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. प्रारूप छह मिश्रण लीवर से बनाया गया है — छँटाई, मूल्य, स्थान, डिजाइन, सेवा, संचार — और वे एक दूसरे के साथ सुसंगत होना चाहिए।

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. स्थिति ग्राहक के मन में उन विकल्पों का परिणाम है; कुछ क्षेत्रों में जानबूझकर कमजोर होना वह है जो आपको दूसरों में मजबूत बनाता है।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **खुदरा रणनीति** — खुदरा विक्रेता के लक्ष्य बाजार का एक कथन, वह प्रारूप जिसे वह उस बाजार की सेवा के लिए उपयोग करेगा, और इसके टिकाऊ प्रतिस्पर्धी लाभ का आधार।

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **लक्ष्य बाजार** — विशिष्ट ग्राहक खंड जिसके प्रति एक खुदरा विक्रेता अपने संसाधन और खुदरा मिश्रण निर्देशित करता है।

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **खुदरा प्रारूप** — खुदरा विक्रेता के प्रस्ताव की प्रकृति, जिसे छँटाई, मूल्य, स्थान, डिजाइन, सेवा और संचार के इसके मिश्रण द्वारा परिभाषित किया गया है।

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **खुदरा मिश्रण** — छह नियंत्रणीय लीवर जो एक खुदरा विक्रेता उस प्रारूप को बनाने के लिए जोड़ता है।

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **स्थिति** — वह छवि जो एक खुदरा विक्रेता ग्राहकों के दिमाग में प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के सापेक्ष कब्जा करता है, इसके खुदरा मिश्रण द्वारा उत्पादित।

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **टिकाऊ प्रतिस्पर्धी लाभ** — एक किनारा जिसे समय के साथ बनाए रखा जा सकता है क्योंकि प्रतिद्वंद्वी इसे आसानी से दोहरा नहीं सकते।

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **Q1 → B.** कीमत में कटौती खुदरा में नकल करने का सबसे आसान कदम है — एक प्रतिद्वंद्वी इसे अगली सुबह मैच कर सकता है, इसलिए यह मात्रा खरीदता है, लाभ नहीं।

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: स्थान, मालिकाना माल, और आपूर्ति-श्रृंखला बुनियादी ढाँचे को दोहराने में सभी को वर्षों और पूंजी की आवश्यकता होती है।

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **Q2 → X (False).** मिश्रण के प्रत्येक तत्व की एक लागत है; गहरी छँटाई और उच्च सेवा लागत संरचना को बढ़ाते हैं, जो सबसे कम कीमत को बनाए रखना असंभव बनाता है।

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: सुसंगत रणनीति के लिए यह चुनना आवश्यक है कि आप कहाँ कमजोर होंगे।

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **Q3 → A.** चौड़ाई (या विविधता) = श्रेणियों की संख्या; गहराई = एक श्रेणी के भीतर SKU की संख्या।

segments.src: Trader Joe's is moderate in breadth and deliberately shallow in depth.*
segments.tr: Trader Joe's चौड़ाई में मध्यम है और गहराई में जानबूझकर उथला है।*

es.title: [Retailing 101 #7] Trader Joe's vende 4.000 artículos. Walmart vende 100.000. Ambos están ganando.

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > Una estrategia minorista es tres decisiones tomadas en conjunto: para quién es, qué venderles y cómo, y por qué esa ventaja seguirá siendo válida en cinco años.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: La mayoría de las personas creen que la estrategia minorista significa "elegir una buena ubicación y no dejarse socavar en precio".

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: Eso son tácticas.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: La estrategia es la capa por encima de eso.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: En los libros de texto de retail, una **estrategia minorista** es una declaración que responde tres preguntas:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **Mercado objetivo** — ¿a qué clientes apuntamos?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **Formato minorista** — ¿qué oferta construiremos para servirles?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **Ventaja competitiva sostenible** — ¿qué hará que sea difícil para los rivales copiarlo?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: La palabra *sostenible* está haciendo trabajo real en la pregunta 3.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: Cualquier competidor puede igualar tu descuento del martes para el miércoles.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: Las ventajas que realmente duran tienden a provenir de un pequeño conjunto de lugares: lealtad y hábito del cliente, ubicaciones físicas que los rivales no pueden obtener, mercancía única que controlas, sistemas de distribución e información, relaciones con proveedores, y cómo contratas y retienes al personal.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: Un corte de precio no está en esa lista.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: El formato en la pregunta 2 se construye a partir de la **mezcla minorista** — los seis controles que tira un minorista, todos los cuales deben apuntar en la misma dirección:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **Surtido de mercancías** — cuántas categorías (amplitud), cuántas opciones dentro de cada una (profundidad)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **Precios** — precio bajo diario, promoción alto-bajo, premium

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **Ubicación** — centro comercial, centro comercial lineal, centro, solo en línea

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **Diseño y exhibición de tienda** — disposición, atmósfera, cuánto puedes llevar en una mano

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Servicio al cliente** — mostrador de ayuda con personal vs. autopago vs. chatbot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Comunicación** — publicidad, correo electrónico, programas de lealtad, redes sociales

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Establece esos seis, y has producido una **posición**: el lugar que tu tienda ocupa en la mente de un comprador en relación a las alternativas.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: El posicionamiento no es un eslogan que escribes.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: Es el residuo de las seis decisiones que realmente tomaste.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: La parte incómoda es que la mezcla tiene que ser *internamente consistente*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Surtido profundo más precios bajos más servicio de alto nivel más bienes raíces de primera no es una estrategia — es una lista de deseos, y pierde dinero.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: Cada minorista fuerte es visiblemente malo en algo a propósito.

segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.tr: Digamos que vives en Columbus, Ohio, y hay cuatro opciones de comestibles dentro de una conducción de quince minutos.

segments.tr: Misma ciudad, mismos compradores, cuatro respuestas completamente diferentes.

segments.tr: Un supermercado convencional lleva 30.000 o más.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: La mayoría de lo que hay en un estante de TJ es su propia marca privada, no hay tarjeta de lealtad, no hay circular semanal, y las tiendas son pequeñas — a menudo en espacios minoristas más antiguos y más baratos en lugar de un nuevo espacio ancla.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: Observa la consistencia: un surtido estrecho significa alto volumen por artículo, lo que significa mejor costo por unidad, lo que financia un precio de $3,99 en algo que se siente especializado.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Su ventaja es mercancía única que literalmente no puedes comprar en otro lugar, más una tienda lo suficientemente pequeña que un viaje completo toma veinte minutos.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: Mercado objetivo: compradores que preferirían tener a alguien más que edite las opciones para ellos.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**, a dos millas de distancia, es aún más estricto.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: Los productos permanecen en la caja de envío, alquilas el carrito con una moneda, embolsas tus propios comestibles y traes tus propias bolsas.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: Cada uno de esos es un costo eliminado y transmitido al precio.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: Objetivo: compradores cuya prioridad principal es el total al pie del recibo.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** va en la dirección opuesta — surtido enorme, comestibles más neumáticos más televisores, precio bajo diario financiado no por un surtido pequeño sino por sistemas de cadena de suministro e información construidos durante décadas.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: Esa es una ventaja medida en miles de millones de dólares en infraestructura, que es exactamente por qué es sostenible.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** cobra más y está bien con eso: alimentos preparados, mostradores con personal, estándares de abastecimiento, ubicaciones en áreas comerciales de ingresos más altos.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Ahora el punto clave.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Ninguno de estos cuatro es "la mejor tienda de comestibles", y ninguno está tratando de vencer a los otros en su propio juego.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's no está perdiendo cuando Walmart tiene un pasillo de cereales más grande — un pasillo estrecho es la estrategia.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: Cuando un minorista *sí* intenta ser los cuatro a la vez, la mezcla se vuelve incoherente, la posición se empaña, y los compradores dejan de poder decir para qué es la tienda.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: Esa es la autopsia habitual de una cadena fallida.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de Tres Líneas

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. Estrategia minorista = mercado objetivo + formato minorista + una ventaja competitiva que es realmente difícil de copiar.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. El formato se construye a partir de seis controles de mezcla — surtido, precio, ubicación, diseño, servicio, comunicación — y deben ser coherentes entre sí.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. El posicionamiento es el resultado de esas decisiones en la mente del cliente; ser deliberadamente débil en algunas áreas es lo que te hace fuerte en otras.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **Estrategia minorista** — Una declaración del mercado objetivo del minorista, el formato que utilizará para servir ese mercado, y la base de su ventaja competitiva sostenible.

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **Mercado objetivo** — El segmento de cliente específico hacia el que un minorista dirige sus recursos y mezcla minorista.

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Formato minorista** — La naturaleza de la oferta del minorista, definida por su mezcla de surtido, precio, ubicación, diseño, servicio, y comunicación.

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **Mezcla minorista** — Los seis controles controlables que un minorista combina para construir ese formato.

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **Posicionamiento** — La imagen que un minorista ocupa en las mentes de los clientes en relación a los competidores, producida por su mezcla minorista.

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **Ventaja competitiva sostenible** — Una ventaja que puede mantenerse en el tiempo porque los rivales no pueden replicarla fácilmente.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **P1 → B.** Un corte de precio es el movimiento más fácil en el retail para copiar — un competidor puede igualarlo a la mañana siguiente, así que compra volumen, no ventaja.

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: Las ubicaciones, la mercancía propietaria, y la infraestructura de la cadena de suministro toman años y capital para replicar.

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **P2 → F (Falso).** Cada elemento de la mezcla tiene un costo; el surtido profundo y el servicio de alto nivel elevan la estructura de costos, lo que hace que el precio más bajo sea imposible de mantener.

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: La estrategia coherente requiere elegir en qué ser débil.

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **P3 → A.** Amplitud (o variedad) = número de categorías; profundidad = número de SKU dentro de una categoría.

segments.src: Trader Joe's is moderate in breadth and deliberately shallow in depth.*
segments.tr: Trader Joe's es moderado en amplitud y deliberadamente superficial en profundidad.*

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > استراتيجية البيع بالتجزئة هي ثلاث قرارات يتم اتخاذها معاً: من تستهدف، وما الذي ستبيعه لهم وكيف، ولماذا ستبقى ميزتك هذه موجودة بعد خمس سنوات.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: يعتقد معظم الناس أن استراتيجية البيع بالتجزئة تعني "اختيار موقع جيد وعدم خفض الأسعار."

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: هذا تكتيك.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: الاستراتيجية هي الطبقة فوقها.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: في كتب البيع بالتجزئة، **استراتيجية البيع بالتجزئة** هي عبارة تجيب عن ثلاثة أسئلة:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **السوق المستهدفة** — أي العملاء نستهدفهم؟

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **صيغة البيع بالتجزئة** — أي عرض سنبنيه لخدمتهم؟

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **الميزة التنافسية المستدامة** — ما الذي سيجعل من الصعب على المنافسين نسخها؟

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: كلمة *المستدامة* تؤدي عملاً حقيقياً في السؤال 3.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: أي منافس يمكنه مطابقة خصمك في يوم الثلاثاء بحلول يوم الأربعاء.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: الميزات التي تدوم فعلاً تميل إلى أن تأتي من مجموعة صغيرة من الأماكن: ولاء العملاء والعادة، والمواقع المادية التي لا يستطيع المنافسون الحصول عليها، والبضائع الفريدة التي تتحكم بها، وأنظمة التوزيع والمعلومات، وعلاقات الموردين، وكيفية توظيفك والاحتفاظ بالموظفين.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: خفض السعر ليس في تلك القائمة.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: يتم بناء الصيغة في السؤال 2 من **مزيج البيع بالتجزئة** — الروافع الستة التي يسحبها بائع التجزئة، وجميعها يجب أن تشير في نفس الاتجاه:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **تشكيلة البضائع** — كم عدد الفئات (العرض)، كم عدد الخيارات داخل كل منها (العمق)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **التسعير** — سعر منخفض يومي، ترويج عالي-منخفض، متميز

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **الموقع** — مول، مركز تجاري، وسط المدينة، عبر الإنترنت فقط

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **تصميم المتجر والعرض** — التخطيط، الجو، كم يمكنك حمله بيد واحدة

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **خدمة العملاء** — مكتب مساعدة موظف مقابل الخروج الذاتي مقابل روبوت الدردشة

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **الاتصال** — الإعلانات، البريد الإلكتروني، برامج الولاء، الوسائط الاجتماعية

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: عند تعيين هذه الستة، تكون قد أنتجت **موضعاً**: المكان الذي يشغله متجرك في ذهن المتسوق بالنسبة للبدائل.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: الموضع ليس شعاراً تكتبه.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: إنها نتيجة الخيارات الستة التي اتخذتها فعلاً.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: الجزء غير المريح هو أن المزيج يجب أن يكون *متسقاً داخلياً*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: تشكيلة عميقة بالإضافة إلى أسعار منخفضة بالإضافة إلى خدمة عالية بالإضافة إلى العقارات الأساسية ليست استراتيجية — إنها قائمة رغبات وتخسر المال.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: كل بائع تجزئة قوي سيء بشكل واضح في شيء ما عن قصد.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.tr: لنفترض أنك تعيش في كولومبوس بولاية أوهايو، وهناك أربعة خيارات بقالة في غضون خمسة عشر دقيقة بالسيارة.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: نفس المدينة، نفس المتسوقين، أربع إجابات مختلفة تماماً.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** تحمل حوالي 4,000 منتج.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: يحمل متجر البقالة التقليدي 30,000 أو أكثر.

segments.tr: معظم ما هو على رف TJ هو علامتها التجارية الخاصة، لا توجد بطاقة ولاء، لا دائرة أسبوعية، والمتاجر صغيرة — غالباً في مساحة بيع بالتجزئة أقدم وأرخص بدلاً من موقع مرساة جديد.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: لاحظ الاتساق: تشكيلة ضيقة تعني حجماً عالياً لكل عنصر، مما يعني تكلفة أفضل لكل وحدة، مما يمول سعر 3.99 دولار على شيء يبدو متخصصاً.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: ميزتهم هي بضائع فريدة لا يمكنك شراؤها حرفياً في مكان آخر، بالإضافة إلى متجر صغير بما يكفي بحيث تستغرق الرحلة الكاملة عشرين دقيقة.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: السوق المستهدفة: المتسوقون الذين يفضلون أن يقوم شخص آخر بتحرير الخيارات لهم.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**، على بعد ميلين، أكثر صرامة.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: تبقى المنتجات في صناديق الشحن، تستأجر السلة بربع دولار، تضع بقالتك في أكياس وتحضر أكيسك الخاصة.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: كل واحد من هؤلاء هو تكلفة تمت إزالتها وتمريرها إلى السعر.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: الهدف: المتسوقون الذين أولويتهم الأساسية هي الإجمالي في أسفل الإيصال.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** تذهب في الاتجاه المعاكس — تشكيلة ضخمة، بقالة بالإضافة إلى إطارات بالإضافة إلى أجهزة تلفاز، سعر منخفض يومي ممول ليس من قبل تشكيلة صغيرة ولكن من قبل سلسلة التوريد وأنظمة المعلومات المبنية على مدى عقود.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: هذه ميزة تقاس بمليارات الدولارات من البنية التحتية، وهذا هو السبب بالضبط في استدامتها.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** تفرض رسوماً أكثر وهي بخير مع ذلك: الأطعمة المحضرة والعدادات الموظفة ومعايير الحصول والمواقع في مناطق تجارية ذات دخل أعلى.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: الآن النقطة الأساسية.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: لا أحد من هؤلاء الأربعة هو "أفضل متجر بقالة"، وأحد منهم لا يحاول هزيمة الآخرين في لعبتهم الخاصة.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's لا تخسر عندما يكون لدى Walmart ممر حبوب أكبر — ممر ضيق هو الاستراتيجية.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: عندما يحاول بائع التجزئة *فعلاً* أن يكون الأربعة في نفس الوقت، يصبح المزيج غير متماسك، والموضع غير واضح، ويتوقف المتسوقون عن القدرة على قول ما هو المتجر.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: هذا هو التشريح المعتاد لسلسلة فاشلة.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. استراتيجية البيع بالتجزئة = السوق المستهدفة + صيغة البيع بالتجزئة + ميزة تنافسية يصعب نسخها فعلاً.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. يتم بناء الصيغة من ستة روافع مزيج — التشكيلة والسعر والموقع والتصميم والخدمة والاتصال — ويجب أن تكون متسقة مع بعضها البعض.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. الموضع هو نتيجة تلك الخيارات في ذهن العميل؛ كونك ضعيفاً عن قصد في بعض المجالات هو ما يجعلك قوياً في مجالات أخرى.

segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: **Q1.** أي من الخيارات التالية هو عموماً أقل *مصدر مستدام* للميزة التنافسية في البيع بالتجزئة؟

segments.src: A.
segments.tr: أ.

segments.src: Prime locations competitors can't obtain
segments.tr: المواقع الأساسية التي لا يمكن للمنافسين الحصول عليها

segments.src: B.
segments.tr: ب.

segments.src: A price cut on a nationally branded product
segments.tr: خفض السعر على منتج ذي علامة تجارية وطنية

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > Une stratégie de détail repose sur trois décisions prises ensemble : pour qui vous êtes, ce que vous leur vendrez et comment, et pourquoi cet avantage perdurera dans cinq ans.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le Concept d'Aujourd'hui

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: La plupart des gens pensent que la stratégie de détail signifie « choisir un bon emplacement et ne pas vous faire surpasser sur le prix ».

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: C'est de la tactique.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: La stratégie est le niveau au-dessus.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: Dans les manuels de détail, une **stratégie de détail** est un énoncé qui répond à trois questions :

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **Marché cible** — quels clients cherchons-nous à atteindre ?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **Format de détail** — quelle offre construirons-nous pour les servir ?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **Avantage concurrentiel durable** — qu'est-ce qui rendra cela difficile à imiter pour nos rivaux ?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: Le mot *durable* joue un rôle réel dans la question 3.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: N'importe quel concurrent peut égaler votre remise du mardi dès mercredi.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: Les avantages qui durent réellement ont tendance à provenir d'un petit ensemble de sources : la fidélité et les habitudes des clients, les emplacements physiques que les rivaux ne peuvent pas obtenir, les marchandises uniques que vous contrôlez, les systèmes de distribution et d'information, les relations avec les fournisseurs, et votre façon de recruter et de fidéliser le personnel.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: Une baisse de prix ne figure pas sur cette liste.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: Le format à la question 2 est construit à partir du **mix de détail** — les six leviers qu'un détaillant actionne, tous doivent pointer dans la même direction :

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **Assortiment de marchandises** — combien de catégories (largeur), combien de choix dans chacune (profondeur)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **Tarification** — prix bas tous les jours, promotion hauts-bas, premium

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **Emplacement** — centre commercial, galerie marchande, centre-ville, en ligne uniquement

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **Conception et présentation du magasin** — disposition, ambiance, ce que vous pouvez porter d'une main

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Service à la clientèle** — comptoir d'aide avec personnel par rapport à l'auto-paiement par rapport au chatbot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Communication** — publicité, email, programmes de fidélité, réseaux sociaux

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Fixez ces six éléments, et vous avez créé une **position** : la place que votre magasin occupe dans l'esprit d'un acheteur par rapport aux alternatives.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: Le positionnement n'est pas un slogan que vous écrivez.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: C'est le résidu des six choix que vous avez réellement faits.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: La partie inconfortable est que le mix doit être *cohérent en interne*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Un assortiment profond plus des prix bas plus un service élevé plus des emplacements de premier plan n'est pas une stratégie — c'est une liste de souhaits, et cela perd de l'argent.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: Chaque détaillant prospère est délibérément mauvais à quelque chose.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la Vie Quotidienne

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: Supposons que vous viviez à Columbus, Ohio, et qu'il y ait quatre options d'épicerie à quinze minutes de route.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: Même ville, mêmes acheteurs, quatre réponses complètement différentes.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** propose environ 4 000 articles.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: Un supermarché conventionnel en propose 30 000 ou plus.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: La plupart de ce qui se trouve sur les étagères de TJ's est sa propre marque propre, il n'y a pas de carte de fidélité, pas de circulaire hebdomadaire, et les magasins sont petits — souvent dans des espaces commerciaux plus anciens et moins chers plutôt que dans un nouvel emplacement de premier plan.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: Remarquez la cohérence : un assortiment étroit signifie un volume élevé par article, ce qui signifie un meilleur coût par unité, ce qui finance un prix de 3,99 $ pour quelque chose qui semble spécialisé.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Leur avantage est une marchandise unique que vous ne pouvez littéralement pas acheter ailleurs, plus un magasin assez petit pour qu'un voyage complet prenne vingt minutes.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: Marché cible : les acheteurs qui préfèrent que quelqu'un d'autre fasse la sélection pour eux.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**, à deux miles de distance, est encore plus strict.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: Les produits restent dans leur carton de livraison, vous louez le chariot avec une pièce de monnaie, vous emballez vos propres courses et apportez vos propres sacs.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: Chacun d'eux est un coût supprimé et répercuté sur le prix.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: Cible : les acheteurs dont la priorité absolue est le total en bas du reçu.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** emprunte la direction opposée — un assortiment énorme, épicerie plus pneus plus téléviseurs, prix bas tous les jours financés non par un petit assortiment mais par les chaînes d'approvisionnement et les systèmes d'information édifiés au cours des décennies.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: C'est un avantage mesuré en milliards de dollars d'infrastructure, c'est exactement pourquoi c'est durable.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** facture plus et cela lui convient : aliments préparés, comptoirs avec personnel, normes d'approvisionnement, emplacements dans des zones commerciales à revenus plus élevés.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Maintenant, le point clé.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Aucune de ces quatre n'est « le meilleur épicier », et aucune n'essaie de battre les autres à leur propre jeu.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's ne perd pas quand Walmart a une allée de céréales plus grande — une allée étroite est la stratégie.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: Quand un détaillant *essaie* d'être les quatre à la fois, le mix devient incohérent, le positionnement s'estompe, et les acheteurs ne peuvent plus dire à quoi sert le magasin.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: C'est l'autopsie habituelle d'une chaîne défaillante.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Résumé en Trois Lignes

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. Stratégie de détail = marché cible + format de détail + un avantage concurrentiel réellement difficile à copier.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. Le format est construit à partir de six leviers du mix — assortiment, prix, emplacement, conception, service, communication — et ils doivent être cohérents les uns avec les autres.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. Le positionnement est le résultat de ces choix dans l'esprit du client ; être délibérément faible dans certains domaines est ce qui vous rend fort dans d'autres.

segments.tr: - **Design e exibição da loja** — layout, atmosfera, quanto você pode carregar em uma mão

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Atendimento ao cliente** — balcão de ajuda atendido vs. checkout automático vs. chatbot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Comunicação** — publicidade, email, programas de fidelidade, redes sociais

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Defina esses seis, e você produziu uma **posição**: o lugar que sua loja ocupa na mente de um comprador em relação às alternativas.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: Posicionamento não é um slogan que você escreve.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: É o resíduo das seis escolhas que você realmente fez.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: A parte desconfortável é que o mix tem que ser *internamente consistente*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Variedade profunda mais preços baixos mais serviço de alta qualidade mais localização de primeira não é uma estratégia — é uma lista de desejos, e perde dinheiro.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: Todo varejista forte é visivelmente ruim em algo propositalmente.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: Digamos que você mora em Columbus, Ohio, e há quatro opções de supermercado em um trajeto de quinze minutos.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: Mesma cidade, mesmos compradores, quatro respostas completamente diferentes.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** oferece aproximadamente 4.000 itens.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: Um supermercado convencional oferece 30.000 ou mais.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: A maioria do que está nas prateleiras da TJ é marca própria, não há cartão de fidelidade, não há encarte semanal, e as lojas são pequenas — geralmente em espaço de varejo antigo e mais barato em vez de um novo espaço principal.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: Observe a consistência: uma variedade estreita significa alto volume por item, o que significa melhor custo por unidade, o que financia um preço de $3,99 em algo que parece especializado.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Sua vantagem é mercadoria exclusiva que você literalmente não pode comprar em outro lugar, além de uma loja pequena o suficiente para que uma viagem completa leve vinte minutos.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: Mercado-alvo: compradores que preferem que alguém escolha as opções para eles.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**, a dois quilômetros de distância, é ainda mais rigoroso.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: Os produtos permanecem nas caixas de embalagem, você aluga o carrinho com uma moeda, você embala suas próprias compras e traz seus próprios sacos.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: Cada um desses é um custo removido e passado para o preço.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: Alvo: compradores cuja prioridade máxima é o total na parte inferior do recibo.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** vai na direção oposta — variedade enorme, mantimentos mais pneus mais TVs, preço baixo diário financiado não por uma variedade pequena, mas por sistemas de distribuição e informação construídos ao longo de décadas.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: Essa é uma vantagem medida em bilhões de dólares de infraestrutura, que é exatamente por que é sustentável.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** cobra mais e fica bem com isso: alimentos preparados, balcões atendidos, padrões de fornecimento, localizações em áreas comerciais de renda mais alta.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Agora o ponto chave.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Nenhum desses quatro é "o melhor supermercado", e nenhum está tentando vencer os outros em seu próprio jogo.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's não está perdendo quando Walmart tem um corredor de cereal maior — um corredor estreito é a estratégia.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: Quando um varejista *tenta* ser os quatro ao mesmo tempo, o mix fica incoerente, a posição fica desfocada e os compradores deixam de conseguir dizer para que serve a loja.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: Essa é a autópsia usual de uma rede fracassada.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. Estratégia de varejo = mercado-alvo + formato de varejo + uma vantagem competitiva que é realmente difícil de copiar.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. O formato é construído a partir de seis alavancas de mix — variedade, preço, localização, design, serviço, comunicação — e devem ser consistentes uns com os outros.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. Posicionamento é o resultado dessas escolhas na mente do cliente; ser deliberadamente fraco em algumas áreas é o que o torna forte em outras.
