segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **Estratégia de varejo** — Uma declaração do mercado-alvo do varejista, o formato que usará para servir esse mercado e a base de sua vantagem competitiva sustentável.

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **Mercado-alvo** — O segmento de cliente específico para o qual um varejista direciona seus recursos e mix de varejo.

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Formato de varejo** — A natureza da oferta do varejista, definida por seu mix de variedade, preço, localização, design, serviço e comunicação.

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **Mix de varejo** — As seis alavancas controláveis que um varejista combina para construir esse formato.

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **Posicionamento** — A imagem que um varejista ocupa na mente dos clientes em relação aos concorrentes, produzida por seu mix de varejo.

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **Vantagem competitiva sustentável** — Uma vantagem que pode ser mantida ao longo do tempo porque rivais não podem replicá-la facilmente.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **Q1 → B.** Um corte de preço é o movimento mais fácil no varejo para copiar — um concorrente pode igualar na manhã seguinte, então compra volume, não vantagem.

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: Localizações, mercadorias proprietárias e infraestrutura de cadeia de suprimentos levam anos e capital para replicar.

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **Q2 → F (Falso).** Cada elemento do mix tem um custo; variedade profunda e serviço de alta qualidade aumentam a estrutura de custos, o que torna o preço mais baixo impossível de sustentar.

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: Estratégia coerente requer escolher em que ser fraco.

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **Q3 → A.** Amplitude (ou variedade) = número de categorias; profundidade = número de SKUs dentro de uma categoria.

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > Strategi ritel adalah tiga keputusan yang dibuat bersama: siapa target Anda, apa yang akan Anda jual kepada mereka dan bagaimana, dan mengapa keunggulan itu akan tetap ada dalam lima tahun.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: Kebanyakan orang berpikir strategi ritel berarti "pilih lokasi yang baik dan jangan undercut harga."

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: Itu adalah taktik.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: Strategi adalah lapisan di atasnya.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: Dalam buku pelajaran ritel, **strategi ritel** adalah pernyataan yang menjawab tiga pertanyaan:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **Pasar target** — pelanggan mana yang kami targetkan?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **Format ritel** — penawaran apa yang akan kami bangun untuk melayani mereka?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **Keunggulan kompetitif berkelanjutan** — apa yang akan membuat itu sulit bagi pesaing untuk meniru?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: Kata *berkelanjutan* melakukan pekerjaan nyata dalam pertanyaan 3.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: Setiap pesaing dapat mencocokkan diskon Selasa Anda pada hari Rabu.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: Keunggulan yang benar-benar bertahan cenderung berasal dari serangkaian tempat kecil: loyalitas dan kebiasaan pelanggan, lokasi fisik yang tidak dapat diperoleh pesaing, barang dagangan unik yang Anda kontrol, sistem distribusi dan informasi, hubungan pemasok, dan cara Anda merekrut dan mempertahankan staf.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: Pemotongan harga tidak ada dalam daftar itu.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: Format dalam pertanyaan 2 dibangun dari **bauran ritel** — enam tuas yang ditarik oleh pengecer, semuanya harus menunjuk ke arah yang sama:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **Penawaran barang dagangan** — berapa banyak kategori (luas), berapa banyak pilihan di setiap kategori (kedalaman)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **Penetapan harga** — harga rendah setiap hari, promosi tinggi-rendah, premium

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **Lokasi** — pusat perbelanjaan, pusat strip, pusat kota, hanya online

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **Desain dan tampilan toko** — tata letak, suasana, berapa banyak yang bisa Anda bawa dengan satu tangan

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Layanan pelanggan** — layanan bantuan dengan staf vs. self-checkout vs. chatbot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Komunikasi** — iklan, email, program loyalitas, media sosial

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Tetapkan keenam hal itu, dan Anda telah menghasilkan **posisi**: tempat yang ditempati toko Anda dalam pikiran pembeli relatif terhadap alternatif.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: Positioning bukan slogan yang Anda tulis.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: Ini adalah sisa dari enam pilihan yang benar-benar Anda buat.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: Bagian yang tidak nyaman adalah bahwa bauran harus *konsisten secara internal*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Penawaran mendalam ditambah harga rendah ditambah layanan tinggi ditambah real estat utama bukanlah strategi — itu adalah daftar keinginan, dan itu kehilangan uang.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: Setiap pengecer yang kuat secara terlihat buruk dalam sesuatu dengan sengaja.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** membawa sekitar 4.000 barang.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: Sebuah supermarket konvensional membawa 30.000 atau lebih.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar apa yang ada di rak TJ adalah label pribadi mereka sendiri, tidak ada kartu loyalitas, tidak ada surat kabar mingguan, dan toko-toko kecil — sering di ruang ritel yang lebih tua dan lebih murah daripada bantalan pengganda baru.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Keunggulan mereka adalah barang dagangan unik yang secara harfiah tidak dapat Anda beli di tempat lain, ditambah toko yang cukup kecil sehingga perjalanan penuh memakan waktu dua puluh menit.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: Itu adalah keunggulan yang diukur dalam miliaran dolar infrastruktur, yang persis mengapa itu berkelanjutan.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Sekarang poin kuncinya.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Tidak ada satu pun dari empat ini adalah "toko kelontong terbaik," dan tidak ada yang mencoba mengalahkan yang lain dalam permainan mereka sendiri.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.tr: 1. Strategi ritel = pasar target + format ritel + keunggulan kompetitif yang benar-benar sulit untuk ditiru.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > 小売戦略は一緒に下される3つの決定である：あなたが誰のためにするのか、彼らに何を売るのか、そしてその優位性が5年後にもまだそこにある理由である。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: ほとんどの人は、小売戦略は「良い場所を選んで価格競争に負けない」という意味だと考えています。

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: それは戦術です。

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: 戦略はそれ以上のレイヤーです。

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: 小売教科書では、**小売戦略**は3つの質問に答える声明です：

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **ターゲット市場** — どの顧客を狙っているのか？

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **小売形式** — 彼らにサービスを提供するためにどのようなオファーを構築しますか？

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **持続可能な競争優位** — ライバルがそれをコピーするのを難しくするのは何か？

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: *持続可能な*という言葉は、質問3で実際の働きをしています。

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: どの競合他社も火曜日の割引を水曜日までに合わせることができます。

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: 実際に続く利点は、小さな場所のセットから来る傾向があります：顧客の忠誠と習慣、ライバルが得られない物理的な場所、あなたが制御するユニークな商品、流通と情報システム、サプライヤーの関係、およびスタッフを雇用して保つ方法。

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: 値下げはそのリストに含まれていません。

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: 質問2の形式は、**小売ミックス**から構築されます — 小売業者が引く6つのレバー、すべてが同じ方向を指す必要があります：

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **商品品揃え** — カテゴリ数（幅）、各カテゴリ内の選択肢数（深さ）

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **価格設定** — 毎日の低価格、高低プロモーション、プレミアム

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **場所** — モール、ストリップセンター、ダウンタウン、オンラインのみ

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **店舗設計と展示** — レイアウト、雰囲気、片手でいくら持ち運べるか

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **カスタマーサービス** — スタッフ付きヘルプデスク対自動チェックアウト対チャットボット

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **コミュニケーション** — 広告、メール、ロイヤリティプログラム、ソーシャル

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: その6つを設定して、**ポジション**を作成しました：代替案に対して買い物客の頭の中で店が占める場所。

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: ポジショニングは書くスローガンではありません。

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: それは実際に行った6つの選択の残りです。

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: 不快な部分は、ミックスが*内部的に一貫性がある*必要があることです。

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: 深い品揃え+低価格+高いサービス+プライム不動産は戦略ではありません — それはウィッシュリストであり、お金を失います。

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: すべての強い小売業者は意図的に何かで明らかに悪いです。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: オハイオ州コロンバスに住んでいると言います、そして15分の運転以内に4つの食料品オプションがあります。

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: 同じ都市、同じ買い物客、4つの完全に異なる答え。

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **トレーダー・ジョーズ**は約4,000商品を扱っています。

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: 従来型のスーパーマーケットは30,000以上を扱っています。

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: TJの棚にあるもののほとんどは独自のプライベートラベルであり、ロイヤリティカードがなく、週刊チラシがなく、店舗は小さいです — 新しいアンカーパッドではなく、古い、安い小売スペースにあることがよくあります。

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: 一貫性に注意してください：狭い品揃えは項目あたりの高いボリュームを意味し、これはユニットあたりより良いコストを意味し、これは特別に感じるものに$3.99の価格をサポートしています。

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: 彼らの利点は、文字通り他の場所で買うことができないユニークな商品であり、さらに完全なトリップが20分かかるほど十分に小さい店です。

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: ターゲット市場：他の誰かに自分の選択を編集してもらいたい買い物客。

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **アルディ**は2マイル離れた場所にあり、さらに厳密です。

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: 製品は配送用段ボールに留まります。四半期でカートを借ります。自分の食料品をバッグに入れて、自分のバッグを持ってきます。

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: それらのそれぞれは、削除された費用であり、価格に渡されます。

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: ターゲット：最優先事項は領収書の下部の合計である買い物客。

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **ウォルマート・スーパーセンター**は逆の方向に進みます — 膨大な品揃え、食料品とタイヤとテレビ、小さな品揃えではなく、数十年にわたって構築されたサプライチェーンと情報システムによって資金を供給された毎日の低価格。

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: それは数十億ドルのインフラストラクチャで測定された利点であり、それは持続可能な理由はまさにそれです。

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **ホールフーズ**はより多く請求し、それで問題ありません：調理済み食品、スタッフ付きカウンター、調達基準、より高い収入の商圏内の場所。

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: 今、重要な点です。

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: これらの4つのどれも「最高の食料品店」ではなく、どれも他のものを自分たちのゲームで打ち負かすことを試みていません。

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: ウォルマートがより大きなシリアルの通路を持っているとき、トレーダー・ジョーズは失っていません — 狭い通路が戦略です。

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: 小売業者が4つすべてになろうとするとき、ミックスは矛盾した、位置がぼやけ、買い物客は店が何のためにあるのかを言うことができなくなります。

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: それは失敗したチェーン上の通常の検査です。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行のリキャップ

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. 小売戦略 = ターゲット市場 + 小売形式 + 実際にコピーしにくい競争上の優位。

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. 形式は6つのミックスレバーから構築されます — 品揃え、価格、場所、設計、サービス、通信 — そして、それらは互いに一貫性がある必要があります。

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. ポジショニングは顧客の心の中のそれらの選択の結果です。いくつかの領域で意図的に弱いことは、他の領域で強いものにするものです。

segments.tr: Das Format in Frage 2 wird aus dem **Einzelhandelsmix** gebaut — den sechs Hebeln, die ein Einzelhändler zieht, die alle in die gleiche Richtung zeigen müssen:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **Warensortiment** — wie viele Kategorien (Breite), wie viele Auswahlmöglichkeiten in jeder (Tiefe)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **Preisgestaltung** — täglich niedriger Preis, High-Low-Aktion, Premium

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **Standort** — Einkaufszentrum, Streifenzentrum, Innenstadt, nur online

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **Ladengestaltung und Display** — Layout, Atmosphäre, wie viel Sie in einer Hand tragen können

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Kundenservice** — Personal-Helpdesk vs. Selbstbedienung vs. Chatbot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Kommunikation** — Werbung, E-Mail, Treueprogramme, soziale Netzwerke

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Legen Sie diese sechs fest, und Sie haben eine **Position** erzeugt: den Platz, den Ihr Geschäft im Kopf eines Käufers im Verhältnis zu den Alternativen einnimmt.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: Positionierung ist kein Slogan, den Sie schreiben.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: Das ist der Rückstand der sechs Entscheidungen, die Sie tatsächlich getroffen haben.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: Das Unangenehme ist, dass der Mix *intern konsistent* sein muss.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Tiefes Sortiment plus niedrige Preise plus hoher Service plus erstklassige Immobilien ist keine Strategie — das ist eine Wunschliste, und sie verliert Geld.

segments.src: Every strong retailer is visibly bad at something on purpose.
segments.tr: Jeder starke Einzelhändler ist bewusst und deutlich schlecht in etwas.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im täglichen Leben

segments.src: Say you live in Columbus, Ohio, and there are four grocery options within a fifteen-minute drive.
segments.tr: Angenommen, Sie leben in Columbus, Ohio, und es gibt vier Lebensmitteloptionen in einer Fahrtzeit von fünfzehn Minuten.

segments.src: Same city, same shoppers, four completely different answers.
segments.tr: Gleiche Stadt, gleiche Käufer, vier völlig unterschiedliche Antworten.

segments.src: **Trader Joe's** carries roughly 4,000 items.
segments.tr: **Trader Joe's** führt ungefähr 4.000 Artikel.

segments.src: A conventional supermarket carries 30,000 or more.
segments.tr: Ein herkömmlicher Supermarkt führt 30.000 oder mehr.

segments.src: Most of what's on a TJ's shelf is its own private label, there's no loyalty card, no weekly circular, and stores are small — often in older, cheaper retail space rather than a new anchor pad.
segments.tr: Das meiste auf einem TJ-Regal ist eine Eigenmarke des Unternehmens, es gibt keine Treuekarte, keinen wöchentlichen Prospekt, und die Geschäfte sind klein — oft in älterer, billigerer Handelsfläche statt auf einem neuen Ankerplatz.

segments.src: Notice the consistency: a narrow assortment means high volume per item, which means better cost per unit, which funds a $3.99 price on something that feels specialty.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie die Konsistenz: ein schmales Sortiment bedeutet hohes Volumen pro Artikel, was bessere Kosten pro Einheit bedeutet, was einen Preis von $3.99 für etwas finanziert, das sich speziell anfühlt.

segments.src: Their advantage is unique merchandise you literally cannot buy elsewhere, plus a store small enough that a full trip takes twenty minutes.
segments.tr: Ihr Vorteil ist einzigartige Ware, die Sie buchstäblich nirgendwo sonst kaufen können, plus ein Geschäft, das klein genug ist, dass ein vollständiger Einkauf zwanzig Minuten dauert.

segments.src: Target market: shoppers who'd rather have someone else edit the choices for them.
segments.tr: Zielmarkt: Käufer, die lieber jemand anderen die Auswahl für sie treffen lassen würden.

segments.src: **Aldi**, two miles away, is stricter still.
segments.tr: **Aldi**, zwei Meilen entfernt, ist noch strenger.

segments.src: Products stay in the shipping carton, you rent the cart with a quarter, you bag your own groceries and bring your own bags.
segments.tr: Produkte bleiben im Versandkarton, Sie mieten den Wagen mit 25 Cent, Sie packen Ihre eigenen Lebensmittel ein und bringen Ihre eigenen Taschen mit.

segments.src: Every one of those is a cost removed and passed into price.
segments.tr: Jeder dieser Punkte ist eine Kostenersparnis, die in den Preis weitergegeben wird.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: Ziel: Käufer, deren oberste Priorität das Total am Ende der Quittung ist.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** geht in die entgegengesetzte Richtung — riesiges Sortiment, Lebensmittel plus Reifen plus Fernseher, täglich niedriger Preis, finanziert nicht durch ein kleines Sortiment, sondern durch Liefer- und Informationssysteme, die über Jahrzehnte aufgebaut wurden.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: Das ist ein Vorteil, der in Milliarden Dollar Infrastruktur gemessen wird, weshalb er nachhaltig ist.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** verlangt mehr und ist damit zufrieden: Fertiggerichte, besetzte Theken, Beschaffungsstandards, Standorte in Handelsbereichen mit höherem Einkommen.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Jetzt der Schlüsselpunkt.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Keiner dieser vier ist "der beste Lebensmittelladen", und keiner versucht, die anderen in ihrem eigenen Spiel zu schlagen.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's verliert nicht, wenn Walmart einen größeren Getreidegang hat — ein schmaler Gang ist die Strategie.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Einzelhändler *versucht*, alle vier gleichzeitig zu sein, wird der Mix inkohärent, die Position verschwimmt, und Käufer können nicht mehr sagen, wofür das Geschäft ist.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: Das ist die übliche Obduktion einer gescheiterten Kette.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. Einzelhandelsstrategie = Zielmarkt + Einzelhandelsformat + ein Wettbewerbsvorteil, der schwer zu kopieren ist.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. Das Format wird aus sechs Hebeln gebaut — Sortiment, Preis, Standort, Design, Service, Kommunikation — und sie müssen miteinander konsistent sein.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. Positionierung ist das Ergebnis dieser Entscheidungen im Kopf des Kunden; bewusst schwach in einigen Bereichen zu sein, ist das, was Sie in anderen stark macht.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **Einzelhandelsstrategie** — Eine Aussage über den Zielmarkt des Einzelhändlers, das Format, das er zur Bedienung dieses Marktes verwendet, und die Grundlage seines nachhaltigen Wettbewerbsvorteil.

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **Zielmarkt** — Das spezifische Kundensegment, auf das ein Einzelhändler seine Ressourcen und seinen Einzelhandelsmix ausrichtet.

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Einzelhandelsformat** — Die Art des Angebots des Einzelhändlers, definiert durch seine Mischung aus Sortiment, Preis, Standort, Design, Service und Kommunikation.

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **Einzelhandelsmix** — Die sechs kontrollierbaren Hebel, die ein Einzelhändler kombiniert, um dieses Format aufzubauen.

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **Positionierung** — Das Bild, das ein Einzelhändler im Kopf von Kunden im Verhältnis zu Konkurrenten einnimmt, erzeugt durch seinen Einzelhandelsmix.

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **Nachhaltiger Wettbewerbsvorteil** — Ein Vorteil, der im Laufe der Zeit beibehalten werden kann, da Konkurrenten ihn nicht leicht replizieren können.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **F1 → B.** Eine Preissenkung ist der einfachste Schachzug im Einzelhandel zu kopieren — ein Konkurrent kann ihn am nächsten Morgen anpassen, so dass es Volumen bringt, keinen Vorteil.

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: Standorte, proprietäre Waren und Supply-Chain-Infrastruktur erfordern alle Jahre und Kapital zum Replizieren.

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **F2 → X (Falsch).** Jedes Element des Mix hat einen Preis; tiefes Sortiment und hoher Service erhöhen die Kostenstruktur, was den niedrigsten Preis unmöglich macht zu halten.

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: Eine kohärente Strategie erfordert zu wählen, worin man schwach sein soll.

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **F3 → A.** Breite (oder Vielfalt) = Anzahl der Kategorien; Tiefe = Anzahl der SKUs in einer Kategorie.

segments.tr: Trader Joe's ist in der Breite moderat und absichtlich flach in der Tiefe.*

segments.src: > A retail strategy is three decisions made together: who you're for, what you'll sell them and how, and why that edge will still be there in five years.
segments.tr: > Chiến lược bán lẻ là ba quyết định được đưa ra cùng nhau: bạn phục vụ ai, bạn sẽ bán cho họ cái gì và như thế nào, và tại sao lợi thế đó sẽ vẫn còn trong năm năm tới.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Most people think retail strategy means "pick a good location and don't get undercut on price."
segments.tr: Hầu hết mọi người nghĩ chiến lược bán lẻ có nghĩa là "chọn vị trí tốt và đừng để giá của bạn bị cắt giảm."

segments.src: That's tactics.
segments.tr: Đó là chiến thuật.

segments.src: Strategy is the layer above it.
segments.tr: Chiến lược là tầng ở trên nó.

segments.src: In retailing textbooks, a **retail strategy** is a statement that answers three questions:
segments.tr: Trong các sách giáo khoa về bán lẻ, **chiến lược bán lẻ** là một tuyên bố trả lời ba câu hỏi:

segments.src: 1. **Target market** — which customers are we aiming at?
segments.tr: 1. **Thị trường mục tiêu** — chúng ta hướng tới khách hàng nào?

segments.src: 2. **Retail format** — what offering will we build to serve them?
segments.tr: 2. **Định dạng bán lẻ** — chúng ta sẽ xây dựng mức độ cung cấp nào để phục vụ họ?

segments.src: 3. **Sustainable competitive advantage** — what will make that hard for rivals to copy?
segments.tr: 3. **Lợi thế cạnh tranh bền vững** — điều gì sẽ làm cho đối thủ cạnh tranh khó sao chép?

segments.src: The word *sustainable* is doing real work in question 3.
segments.tr: Từ *bền vững* đang thực hiện công việc thực sự trong câu hỏi 3.

segments.src: Any competitor can match your Tuesday discount by Wednesday.
segments.tr: Bất kỳ đối thủ cạnh tranh nào cũng có thể sao chép chiết khấu Thứ Ba của bạn vào Thứ Tư.

segments.src: Advantages that actually last tend to come from a small set of places: customer loyalty and habit, physical locations rivals can't get, unique merchandise you control, distribution and information systems, supplier relationships, and how you hire and keep staff.
segments.tr: Những lợi thế thực sự tồn tại lâu dài có xu hướng đến từ một tập hợp nhỏ các địa điểm: lòng trung thành và thói quen của khách hàng, các vị trí vật lý mà đối thủ cạnh tranh không thể đạt được, hàng hóa độc đáo bạn kiểm soát, hệ thống phân phối và thông tin, mối quan hệ với nhà cung cấp, và cách bạn tuyển dụng và giữ chân nhân viên.

segments.src: A price cut isn't on that list.
segments.tr: Một mức giá cắt giảm không nằm trong danh sách đó.

segments.src: The format in question 2 gets built out of the **retail mix** — the six levers a retailer pulls, all of which have to point the same direction:
segments.tr: Định dạng trong câu hỏi 2 được xây dựng từ **hỗn hợp bán lẻ** — sáu đòn bẩy mà một nhà bán lẻ kéo, tất cả đều phải chỉ cùng một hướng:

segments.src: - **Merchandise assortment** — how many categories (breadth), how many choices inside each (depth)
segments.tr: - **Phân loại hàng hóa** — có bao nhiêu danh mục (rộng), có bao nhiêu lựa chọn trong mỗi danh mục (sâu)

segments.src: - **Pricing** — everyday low price, high-low promotion, premium
segments.tr: - **Định giá** — giá thấp hàng ngày, khuyến mại cao-thấp, cao cấp

segments.src: - **Location** — mall, strip center, downtown, online-only
segments.tr: - **Vị trí** — trung tâm mua sắm, trung tâm dải, khu trung tâm thành phố, chỉ trực tuyến

segments.src: - **Store design and display** — layout, atmosphere, how much you can carry in one hand
segments.tr: - **Thiết kế và trưng bày cửa hàng** — bố cục, không khí, bạn có thể mang bao nhiêu bằng một tay

segments.src: - **Customer service** — staffed help desk vs. self-checkout vs. chat bot
segments.tr: - **Dịch vụ khách hàng** — bàn trợ giúp có nhân viên so với tự thanh toán so với trò chuyện bot

segments.src: - **Communication** — advertising, email, loyalty programs, social
segments.tr: - **Giao tiếp** — quảng cáo, email, chương trình khách hàng thân thiết, mạng xã hội

segments.src: Set those six, and you've produced a **position**: the place your store occupies in a shopper's head relative to the alternatives.
segments.tr: Đặt sáu điều đó, và bạn đã tạo ra một **vị trí**: nơi cửa hàng của bạn chiếm trong tâm trí của một người mua sắm so với các lựa chọn thay thế.

segments.src: Positioning isn't a slogan you write.
segments.tr: Định vị không phải là một khẩu hiệu bạn viết.

segments.src: It's the residue of the six choices you actually made.
segments.tr: Đó là phần dư của sáu lựa chọn bạn thực sự đã đưa ra.

segments.src: The uncomfortable part is that the mix has to be *internally consistent*.
segments.tr: Phần khó chịu là hỗn hợp phải *nhất quán nội bộ*.

segments.src: Deep assortment plus low prices plus high service plus prime real estate is not a strategy — it's a wish list, and it loses money.
segments.tr: Phân loại sâu cộng với giá thấp cộng với dịch vụ cao cộng với bất động sản chủ yếu không phải là một chiến lược — nó là một danh sách mong muốn, và nó mất tiền.

segments.src: Target: shoppers whose top priority is the total at the bottom of the receipt.
segments.tr: Mục tiêu: những người mua sắm có ưu tiên hàng đầu là tổng số ở dưới cùng của biên lai.

segments.src: **Walmart Supercenter** goes the opposite way — enormous assortment, groceries plus tires plus TVs, everyday low price funded not by a small assortment but by supply chain and information systems built over decades.
segments.tr: **Walmart Supercenter** đi theo hướng ngược lại — phân loại khổng lồ, tạp hóa cộng với lốp xe cộng với TV, giá thấp hàng ngày được tài trợ không phải bằng phân loại nhỏ mà bằng chuỗi cung ứng và hệ thống thông tin được xây dựng trong nhiều thập kỷ.

segments.src: That's an advantage measured in billions of dollars of infrastructure, which is exactly why it's sustainable.
segments.tr: Đó là một lợi thế được đo bằng hàng tỷ đô la cơ sở hạ tầng, đó chính xác là lý do tại sao nó bền vững.

segments.src: **Whole Foods** charges more and is fine with that: prepared foods, staffed counters, sourcing standards, locations in higher-income trade areas.
segments.tr: **Whole Foods** tính phí cao hơn và không sao với điều đó: thực phẩm chế biến sẵn, quầy có nhân viên, tiêu chuẩn nguồn gốc, vị trí trong các khu vực thương mại thu nhập cao hơn.

segments.src: Now the key point.
segments.tr: Bây giờ là điểm chính.

segments.src: None of these four is "the best grocery store," and none is trying to beat the others at their own game.
segments.tr: Không ai trong bốn người này là "cửa hàng tạp hóa tốt nhất", và không ai cố gắng đánh bại những người khác trong trò chơi của riêng họ.

segments.src: Trader Joe's isn't losing when Walmart has a bigger cereal aisle — a narrow aisle is the strategy.
segments.tr: Trader Joe's không thua khi Walmart có một lối đi ngũ cốc lớn hơn — một lối đi hẹp là chiến lược.

segments.src: When a retailer *does* try to be all four at once, the mix goes incoherent, the position blurs, and shoppers stop being able to say what the store is for.
segments.tr: Khi một nhà bán lẻ *có* cố gắng là cả bốn cùng một lúc, hỗn hợp trở nên không nhất quán, vị trí mất đi, và những người mua sắm không thể nói được cửa hàng dùng để làm gì.

segments.src: That's the usual autopsy on a failed chain.
segments.tr: Đó là tử tiết thường lệ trên một chuỗi thất bại.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt Ba Dòng

segments.src: 1. Retail strategy = target market + retail format + a competitive advantage that's actually hard to copy.
segments.tr: 1. Chiến lược bán lẻ = thị trường mục tiêu + định dạng bán lẻ + lợi thế cạnh tranh thực sự khó sao chép.

segments.src: 2. The format is built from six mix levers — assortment, price, location, design, service, communication — and they must be consistent with each other.
segments.tr: 2. Định dạng được xây dựng từ sáu đòn bẩy hỗn hợp — phân loại, giá, vị trí, thiết kế, dịch vụ, giao tiếp — và chúng phải nhất quán với nhau.

segments.src: 3. Positioning is the result of those choices in the customer's mind; being deliberately weak in some areas is what makes you strong in others.
segments.tr: 3. Định vị là kết quả của những lựa chọn đó trong tâm trí của khách hàng; có chủ ý yếu ớt ở một số khu vực là điều làm cho bạn mạnh mẽ ở những khu vực khác.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Điều Khoản Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Retail strategy** — A statement of the retailer's target market, the format it will use to serve that market, and the basis of its sustainable competitive advantage.
segments.tr: - **Chiến lược bán lẻ** — Một tuyên bố về thị trường mục tiêu của nhà bán lẻ, định dạng nó sẽ sử dụng để phục vụ thị trường đó, và cơ sở của lợi thế cạnh tranh bền vững của nó.

segments.src: - **Target market** — The specific customer segment a retailer directs its resources and retail mix toward.
segments.tr: - **Thị trường mục tiêu** — Phân khúc khách hàng cụ thể mà nhà bán lẻ hướng tài nguyên và hỗn hợp bán lẻ của nó.

segments.src: - **Retail format** — The nature of the retailer's offering, defined by its mix of assortment, price, location, design, service, and communication.
segments.tr: - **Định dạng bán lẻ** — Bản chất của mức độ cung cấp của nhà bán lẻ, được định nghĩa bởi hỗn hợp phân loại, giá, vị trí, thiết kế, dịch vụ và giao tiếp của nó.

segments.src: - **Retail mix** — The six controllable levers a retailer combines to build that format.
segments.tr: - **Hỗn hợp bán lẻ** — Sáu đòn bẩy có thể kiểm soát được mà nhà bán lẻ kết hợp để xây dựng định dạng đó.

segments.src: - **Positioning** — The image a retailer occupies in customers' minds relative to competitors, produced by its retail mix.
segments.tr: - **Định vị** — Hình ảnh mà nhà bán lẻ chiếm trong tâm trí của khách hàng so với đối thủ cạnh tranh, được tạo ra bởi hỗn hợp bán lẻ của nó.

segments.src: - **Sustainable competitive advantage** — An edge that can be maintained over time because rivals can't easily replicate it.
segments.tr: - **Lợi thế cạnh tranh bền vững** — Một lợi thế có thể được duy trì theo thời gian vì đối thủ cạnh tranh không thể dễ dàng sao chép nó.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 → B.** A price cut is the easiest move in retail to copy — a competitor can match it the next morning, so it buys volume, not advantage.
segments.tr: *Câu trả lời: **Q1 → B.** Cắt giảm giá là động thái dễ nhất trong bán lẻ để sao chép — một đối thủ cạnh tranh có thể sao chép nó vào sáng hôm sau, vì vậy nó mua khối lượng, không phải lợi thế.

segments.src: Locations, proprietary merchandise, and supply-chain infrastructure all take years and capital to replicate.
segments.tr: Vị trí, hàng hóa độc quyền và cơ sở hạ tầng chuỗi cung ứng đều mất nhiều năm và vốn để sao chép.

segments.src: **Q2 → X (False).** Each element of the mix has a cost; deep assortment and high service raise the cost structure, which makes the lowest price impossible to sustain.
segments.tr: **Q2 → X (Sai).** Mỗi yếu tố của hỗn hợp đều có chi phí; phân loại sâu và dịch vụ cao nâng cao cấu trúc chi phí, điều này làm cho giá thấp nhất không thể duy trì.

segments.src: Coherent strategy requires choosing what to be weak at.
segments.tr: Chiến lược nhất quán yêu cầu chọn những gì để yếu ớt.

segments.src: **Q3 → A.** Breadth (or variety) = number of categories; depth = number of SKUs within a category.
segments.tr: **Q3 → A.** Rộng (hoặc đa dạng) = số lượng danh mục; sâu = số lượng SKU trong một danh mục.

segments.src: Trader Joe's is moderate in breadth and deliberately shallow in depth.*
segments.tr: Trader Joe's là vừa phải về rộng và có chủ ý nông về sâu.*
